name: Tracxn Technologies Ltd
title: Tracxn Technologies Ltd - 543638 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs21.3 crore, up 1.1% QoQ with EBITDA negative Rs5.9 crore as management invests in sales capacity; no supply-side capacity signal, and the prior FY27 guidance was not repeated.

guidance.value: return to low single digits after one-time step-up

red_flags.label: Negative EBITDA and PAT, FCF negative Rs6.1 crore in H1
red_flags.quote: FCF for H1 was negative 6.1 crore

summary.headline: Tracxn Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 1.1% QoQ to ₹21.3 crore, with EBITDA at negative ₹5.9 crore as investment continues.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations in Q2 FY27 was ₹21.3 crore, up 1.1% QoQ, while EBITDA was negative ₹5.9 crore and PAT negative ₹4.1 crore, including non-cash ESOP charges. Management said margins did not expand in Q2 because it is investing in sales capacity and product, and it framed this as a one-time step-up. Paying customer accounts rose 13% YoY to 2,419 and users rose 16% to 6,854. The company said revenue growth has accelerated to about 7% QoQ (roughly 30% annualised), and it expanded closing-sales headcount to 56 of a planned 60.

segments.name: India vs international
segments.commentary: 48% of H1 FY27 revenue came from outside India across 50 countries; top five markets are US, UK, Singapore and Germany.

segments.name: International (geography unit)
segments.commentary: Revenue from the international unit has grown at roughly 20% in H1 and about 30% annualised on the latest quarter's 7% QoQ rate, per management.

segments.name: Corporate sales
segments.commentary: Corporate sales, which serves corporates for business-development use cases, grew 23% in Q2 per management; a corporate-sales vertical is growing about 20% YoY in the answer to a question.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: 49% of customers are private-market investors (VCs, PE, banks, family offices, accelerators, incubators) and 45% are corporates; the rest are educational institutes and government agencies.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the one-time step-up in investment to be completed over one to two quarters, after which EBITDA margin is expected to return to low single digits.
Closing-sales headcount is planned to reach about 60 by end of December 2026, from 56 onboarded as of September.

Management said historically margins improve quickly when revenue accelerates, with EBITDA conversion of up to 80% on incremental revenue, and expects a non-linear EBITDA expansion if growth keeps accelerating.
Management said the international unit will follow the India playbook at a slightly earlier stage, with one or two units showing early signs over the next quarter or so.
capex_capacity: Closing-sales capacity was planned to double from 34 at the start of the year to 60 by end-December 2026; 56 were onboarded by September.
Sales and marketing is about 30% of headcount, up 25% in the quarter, reflecting a shift toward sales-led growth.
Management said the company is adding automation and AI in its production infrastructure so it can scale without significantly increasing production headcount.

Management said the company is investing in data (cap tables, shareholding, regulatory and legal entity coverage), with UK entity coverage raised to 5.2 million entities, up 16x since March 2025 (figure as stated).
demand_pricing: Management said transaction activity and deal volume are at a 10-year low in India and globally, while funding dollars are rising on mega AI rounds and M&A is recovering to the second-highest level after 2021.
Customer-account growth of 13% outpaced revenue growth, which management attributed to a mix shift toward newer, lower-priced customers in newer geographies; ASP is lower in these segments.
Win rates in the BU rose after the three-phase playbook was applied, and new-customer acquisition reached about 20 a month, double the starting rate, per management.
Management said universities are a single-digit percentage of revenue but serve as a marketing funnel; Tracxn lists IIMs and Stanford among customers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from universities, and is it growing strongly?
qa_highlights.answer: Universities are a single-digit percentage of revenue; management described them as a strategic marketing funnel, citing IIMs and Stanford as customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue been flat at about ₹20 crore per quarter since 2023?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its largest segment, investment banking, slowed with transaction volumes at a 10-year low, so it changed the mix toward VC and corporate offerings; geography growth is about 30% annualised, and customer-account growth is outpacing revenue due to lower ASP in newer segments.

qa_highlights.question: How does the offering differ for IB versus VC clients, and what is the breakdown of free accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: VCs prioritise sector, while IBs prioritise revenue size and Live Deals; the company added data for banks to meet this. Paid-customer count excludes free users; management said it counts accounts as customers and users separately.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company connect with enterprise procurement and supply-chain teams, and how is it handling sales travel?
qa_highlights.answer: Most sales happen remotely from India-based teams, with regional teams in Japan, Singapore, UK and Germany; management said visits are few and buyers at current price points buy remotely.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not building enterprise-focused features given competition from CB Insights and Harmonic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said corporates are a priority; M&A and BD teams are the focus, with product offerings being built, and early customer response expected within two to three quarters. An AI Scout agent is being built for self-serve research.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company convert shared logins into upgrades?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IP-location data flags shared logins, which triggers the upgrade team to offer seats or a full-team pack; management said a large share of upgrades comes from this, without quantifying it.

risks_watch: Margins stay negative until the investment step-up completes; watch whether EBITDA turns positive after the one-to-two-quarter period.
Deal volumes at a 10-year low in India and globally; revenue depends on recovery in transaction and fundraising activity.
Lower-priced new accounts are lifting customer count faster than revenue; watch ASP and whether revenue growth catches up to the 7% QoQ run-rate.
Enterprise and corporate offering is early; management expects proof of response within two to three quarters.
Competition from larger platforms such as CB Insights and Harmonic, per an analyst question.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth acceleration and product momentum, but openly cautious on profitability: management said margins did not expand in Q2 by design. Answers on IB and universities were direct, while questions on enterprise strategy and competition were answered with general commitments and no numbers.
key_quotes: We closed September at 2,419 accounts, a 13% increase.

adds.what: Closing-sales capacity: headcount doubling from 34 to 60 by end-December 2026 (56 onboarded by September)

growth.why: Management says revenue growth accelerated to ~7% QoQ (~30% annualised) and expects EBITDA margin to return to low single digits within one to two quarters as sales headcount goes from 56 to a planned 60 by December 2026; the brief gives no explicit revenue growth guidance, and the 30% run-rate is a quarterly extrapolation, not a guided number.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: after 1-2 quarters (Q4 FY27 to Q1 FY28)
rows.why: Management guided EBITDA margin back to low single digits once the one-time step-up completes over 1-2 quarters, from Q2 FY27 EBITDA of negative ₹5.9 crore on ₹21.3 crore revenue; the claimed up-to-80% incremental conversion is management's historical figure, not guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Closing-sales headcount is planned to go from 56 (Sept) to about 60 by end-December 2026, doubling from 34 at the start of the year; this is people capacity, not plants or physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Paying customer accounts rose 13% YoY to 2,419 and users 16% to 6,854, with new-customer acquisition at about 20 a month (double the starting rate), though revenue grew only 1.1% QoQ in Q2.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or volume guidance was given; the brief's ~30% annualised run-rate is management's extrapolation of one quarter's 7% QoQ growth, not a raised guide, and transaction volumes are at a 10-year low.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margins stay negative until the investment step-up completes, and deal volumes are at a 10-year low in India and globally, so the low-single-digit margin return depends on revenue catching up to the 7% QoQ run-rate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Enterprise and corporate product offerings are being built with early customer response expected within two to three quarters, and an AI Scout agent is in development, but no launch date or revenue figure was given.

rows.label: Automation and AI to scale production without adding headcount
rows.why: Management said it is adding automation and AI to production infrastructure to scale without significantly increasing production headcount, but gave no cost figure.

rows.label: International unit follows India playbook
rows.why: International revenue grew about 20% in H1 and about 30% annualised on the latest 7% QoQ rate, with one or two units expected to show early signs over the next quarter or so; 48% of H1 revenue is from outside India.
